quests.definition: 'Turn up' can also mean to arrive somewhere, often unexpectedly, a completely different meaning from the 'increase volume' sense you already know. The pattern of missed meetings is the clue pointing to arrival here.
quests.exampleSentence: After missing the last three meetings, he finally turned UP this morning.
quests.example: After missing the last three meetings, he finally turned UP this morning.
quests.particleInsight: The particle 'UP' combines with the verb 'TURN' to specialize or transform its action.
quests.literalVsFigurative: Figurative: nothing physically turns — the phrase describes someone appearing after a period of absence or uncertainty.
quests.nativeTip: This means arriving somewhere, often unexpectedly or after being absent.

quests.definition: 'Roll up' is a very informal, casual way to describe arriving somewhere, often suggesting a relaxed, unbothered attitude, sometimes about being late.
quests.exampleSentence: He just rolled UP twenty minutes late, like it was no big deal.
quests.example: He just rolled UP twenty minutes late, like it was no big deal.
quests.particleInsight: The particle 'UP' combines with the verb 'ROLL' to specialize or transform its action.
quests.literalVsFigurative: Figurative, borrowing the casual image of someone strolling in nonchalantly, as if rolling into a scene.
quests.nativeTip: This means arriving somewhere in a very casual, relaxed way, often late.

quests.definition: 'Shown up' is neutral and appropriate for formal writing, unlike 'rolled up,' which sounds far too casual for an official incident report. 'Turned up' would also be understood, but 'shown up' is the safest, most standard choice in formal registers.
quests.exampleSentence: In his formal incident report, the security guard wrote that an unauthorized visitor had SHOWN UP at the loading dock without identification.
quests.example: In his formal incident report, the security guard wrote that an unauthorized visitor had SHOWN UP at the loading dock without identification.
quests.particleInsight: The particle 'SHOWN UP' combines with the verb 'SHOW' to specialize or transform its action.
quests.literalVsFigurative: Figurative, as before — the phrase simply describes someone's unexpected arrival, expressed here in neutral, professional language.
quests.nativeTip: This means arriving, expressed in a plain, neutral way suitable for formal writing.
quests.visualAnchor: 🗝️ SHOW + SHOWN UP ➔ SHOW SHOWN UP

quests.definition: 'Pack it in' means to quit or stop doing something for good, often a job or routine, expressed in a relaxed, informal way rarely used in professional writing.
quests.exampleSentence: After thirty years, she decided to pack it IN and retire to the countryside.
quests.example: After thirty years, she decided to pack it IN and retire to the countryside.
quests.particleInsight: The particle 'IN' combines with the verb 'PACK' to specialize or transform its action.
quests.literalVsFigurative: Figurative, borrowing the image of packing your things away for the last time before leaving something behind entirely.
quests.nativeTip: This means quitting or stopping something completely, in a very casual, conversational tone.

quests.definition: 'Step down' is the standard, formal choice for a resignation letter, unlike 'pack it in,' which would sound jarringly casual in that context. 'Give up' is too vague and general for describing leaving a specific position.
quests.exampleSentence: In her formal resignation letter, she explained that she wished to STEP DOWN from her position as director.
quests.example: In her formal resignation letter, she explained that she wished to STEP DOWN from her position as director.
quests.particleInsight: The particle 'STEP DOWN' combines with the verb 'STEP' to specialize or transform its action.
quests.literalVsFigurative: Figurative, as before — the phrase compares leaving a position of authority to descending from a higher level, expressed here in formal language.
quests.nativeTip: This means resigning from a position, expressed in language suitable for a formal letter.
quests.visualAnchor: 🗝️ STEP + STEP DOWN ➔ STEP STEP DOWN

quests.definition: This reinforces 'pack it in,' describing a stubborn refusal to ever fully retire, in the same relaxed, conversational register introduced earlier in this level.
quests.exampleSentence: My grandad always said he'd never pack it IN , even at eighty-five.
quests.example: My grandad always said he'd never pack it IN , even at eighty-five.
quests.particleInsight: The particle 'IN' combines with the verb 'PACK' to specialize or transform its action.
quests.literalVsFigurative: Figurative, as before — the phrase describes stopping an activity completely, expressed in casual, everyday language.
quests.nativeTip: This means never quitting, expressed in the same casual tone as earlier in this level.

quests.definition: 'Let go' is a common, somewhat euphemistic way to describe an employee being dismissed, often for reasons like budget cuts rather than personal fault.
quests.exampleSentence: Due to budget cuts, twenty employees were let GO last month.
quests.example: Due to budget cuts, twenty employees were let GO last month.
quests.particleInsight: The particle 'GO' combines with the verb 'LET' to specialize or transform its action.
quests.literalVsFigurative: Figurative: nothing physical is released — the phrase softens the harshness of dismissal into gentler, more formal language.
quests.nativeTip: This means dismissing someone from their job, often used as a softer, more formal alternative to 'fired.'

quests.definition: This reviews 'let down,' meaning to disappoint someone, distinct from 'let go' (dismiss from a job) and 'let off' (excuse from punishment) — all part of the same LET family with very different meanings.
quests.exampleSentence: After promising to help, I really didn't want to let her DOWN by canceling at the last minute.
quests.example: After promising to help, I really didn't want to let her DOWN by canceling at the last minute.
quests.particleInsight: The particle 'DOWN' combines with the verb 'LET' to specialize or transform its action.
quests.literalVsFigurative: Figurative, as before — the phrase compares disappointing someone to letting them fall after relying on your support.
quests.nativeTip: This means disappointing someone by failing to follow through on a promise.

quests.definition: 'Let off' means to excuse someone from punishment, often with a lighter consequence than expected, such as a warning instead of a fine. It completes a small family alongside 'let go' and 'let down.'
quests.exampleSentence: The judge decided to let him OFF with just a warning, given it was a first offense.
quests.example: The judge decided to let him OFF with just a warning, given it was a first offense.
quests.particleInsight: The particle 'OFF' combines with the verb 'LET' to specialize or transform its action.
quests.literalVsFigurative: Figurative: nothing is physically released — the phrase describes a punishment being reduced or waived.
quests.nativeTip: This means excusing someone from a punishment they might otherwise have received.

quests.definition: 'Come clean (about something)' means to finally admit the full truth, especially after a period of dishonesty or hiding something significant.
quests.exampleSentence: After weeks of lying, he finally decided to come CLEAN about what really happened.
quests.example: After weeks of lying, he finally decided to come CLEAN about what really happened.
quests.particleInsight: The particle 'CLEAN' combines with the verb 'COME' to specialize or transform its action.
quests.literalVsFigurative: Figurative, borrowing the image of washing away the dirt of dishonesty by finally telling the whole truth.
quests.nativeTip: This means finally telling the full truth after a period of lying.

quests.definition: 'Came clean' fits a dramatic, full confession after months of serious secret deception. 'Owned up' would suit admitting one specific, smaller mistake, and doesn't carry the same sense of finally revealing a long-hidden truth.
quests.exampleSentence: After months of secretly gambling away the family savings, he finally sat everyone down and CAME CLEAN.
quests.example: After months of secretly gambling away the family savings, he finally sat everyone down and CAME CLEAN.
quests.particleInsight: The particle 'CAME CLEAN' combines with the verb 'COME' to specialize or transform its action.
quests.literalVsFigurative: Figurative, as before — the phrase describes finally revealing a truth that had been deliberately hidden for a long time.
quests.nativeTip: This means confessing fully after a long period of serious, hidden deception.
quests.visualAnchor: 🗝️ COME + CAME CLEAN ➔ COME CAME CLEAN

quests.definition: This reinforces 'come clean,' showing that the phrase applies to organizations as well as individuals, especially after years of concealing a serious problem.
quests.exampleSentence: The company was pressured to come CLEAN about the safety issues it had been hiding for years.
quests.example: The company was pressured to come CLEAN about the safety issues it had been hiding for years.
quests.particleInsight: The particle 'CLEAN' combines with the verb 'COME' to specialize or transform its action.
quests.literalVsFigurative: Figurative, as before — the phrase describes finally admitting a truth that had been hidden for a long time.
quests.nativeTip: This means an organization finally admitting to something it had concealed for a long time.

quests.conceptTitle: Phrasal Anatomy: TAKE take it off
quests.definition: 'Take off' is separable, so with a pronoun object like 'it,' the particle must follow the pronoun: 'take it off,' never 'take off it.' This word-order rule applies to many two-word phrasal verbs you've already learned.
quests.exampleSentence: It's warm in here — why don't you take it off?
quests.example: It's warm in here — why don't you take it off?
quests.particleInsight: The particle 'take it off' combines with the verb 'TAKE' to specialize or transform its action.
quests.literalVsFigurative: This question tests grammar rather than meaning — 'take off' still means removing clothing; only the pronoun's position is being tested.
quests.nativeTip: This reviews 'take off' with a pronoun object — remember, pronouns must sit between the verb and the particle.
quests.visualAnchor: 🗝️ TAKE + take it off ➔ TAKE take it off

quests.conceptTitle: Phrasal Anatomy: LOOK look after him
quests.definition: 'Look after' is non-separable, meaning the particle 'after' always stays right next to 'look,' with the object — pronoun or noun — following afterward: 'look after him,' never 'look him after.'
quests.exampleSentence: The dog needs feeding twice a day — can you look after him while we're away?
quests.example: The dog needs feeding twice a day — can you look after him while we're away?
quests.particleInsight: The particle 'look after him' combines with the verb 'LOOK' to specialize or transform its action.
quests.literalVsFigurative: This question tests grammar rather than meaning — 'look after' still means taking care of someone; only the correct fixed word order is being tested.
quests.nativeTip: This reviews 'look after' with a pronoun object — unlike separable verbs, this particle never moves.
quests.visualAnchor: 🗝️ LOOK + look after him ➔ LOOK look after him

quests.conceptTitle: Phrasal Anatomy: SORT sort it out
quests.definition: 'Sort out' is separable, so with a pronoun object like 'it,' the particle follows the pronoun: 'sort it out,' never 'sort out it.' This is the same pattern you saw with 'take it off.'
quests.exampleSentence: There's a problem with the invoice — I'll sort it out tomorrow.
quests.example: There's a problem with the invoice — I'll sort it out tomorrow.
quests.particleInsight: The particle 'sort it out' combines with the verb 'SORT' to specialize or transform its action.
quests.literalVsFigurative: This question tests grammar rather than meaning — 'sort out' still means resolving a problem; only the pronoun's position is being tested.
quests.nativeTip: This reviews 'sort out' with a pronoun object — remember the separable word-order pattern from earlier questions.
quests.visualAnchor: 🗝️ SORT + sort it out ➔ SORT sort it out

quests.definition: 'Break down (something)' can mean to divide it into smaller, clearer components, such as splitting a total cost into categories. This is a transitive use — it takes a direct object — different from the intransitive uses you've already learned, like a machine breaking down on its own.
quests.exampleSentence: Can you break DOWN the total cost into separate categories for the report?
quests.example: Can you break DOWN the total cost into separate categories for the report?
quests.particleInsight: The particle 'DOWN' combines with the verb 'BREAK' to specialize or transform its action.
quests.literalVsFigurative: Figurative: nothing physically splits apart — the phrase describes organizing information into clearer, smaller components.
quests.nativeTip: This means dividing something, like a cost or a report, into smaller, clearer parts.

quests.definition: This reinforces the transitive, 'itemize' sense of 'break down,' here applied to splitting an annual budget into monthly figures for easier review.
quests.exampleSentence: The finance team carefully broke DOWN the annual budget into monthly figures so it would be easier to review.
quests.example: The finance team carefully broke DOWN the annual budget into monthly figures so it would be easier to review.
quests.particleInsight: The particle 'DOWN' combines with the verb 'BREAK' to specialize or transform its action.
quests.literalVsFigurative: Figurative, as before — the phrase describes organizing a large figure into smaller, clearer parts.
quests.nativeTip: This means dividing an annual figure into smaller, more manageable time periods.

quests.definition: This contrasts with the transitive sense earlier in this level — here, 'broke down' is intransitive, describing the projector failing on its own, with no direct object involved.
quests.exampleSentence: Right in the middle of the presentation, the projector suddenly broke DOWN, leaving everyone in the dark.
quests.example: Right in the middle of the presentation, the projector suddenly broke DOWN, leaving everyone in the dark.
quests.particleInsight: The particle 'DOWN' combines with the verb 'BREAK' to specialize or transform its action.
quests.literalVsFigurative: Literal: the projector genuinely stops functioning, unrelated to the figurative 'itemize' sense taught earlier in this level.
quests.nativeTip: This means a machine failing on its own, without anyone deliberately doing anything to it.

quests.definition: 'Set out' can also mean to clearly present information in a structured way, especially in writing, a different sense from 'begin a journey,' which you learned much earlier in this curriculum.
quests.exampleSentence: The proposal sets OUT three clear objectives for the coming year.
quests.example: The proposal sets OUT three clear objectives for the coming year.
quests.particleInsight: The particle 'OUT' combines with the verb 'SET' to specialize or transform its action.
quests.literalVsFigurative: Figurative: nothing is physically arranged — the phrase describes organizing ideas clearly within a document.
quests.nativeTip: This means clearly presenting or stating something, such as objectives in a written proposal.

quests.definition: 'Lay out (something)' means to clearly present a plan, set of expectations, or set of options to others, often at the start of a project or meeting.
quests.exampleSentence: The manager laid OUT her expectations for the project at the very first meeting.
quests.example: The manager laid OUT her expectations for the project at the very first meeting.
quests.particleInsight: The particle 'OUT' combines with the verb 'LAY' to specialize or transform its action.
quests.literalVsFigurative: Figurative, borrowing the image of laying items out on a table so everyone can see them clearly at once.
quests.nativeTip: This means clearly presenting expectations or a plan to other people.

quests.definition: 'Spell out' fits explicit, unambiguous detail, matching 'rather than leaving things vague.' 'Lay out' would suit presenting a general plan, and 'set out' fits formal written statements — neither implies quite the same total clarity as 'spell out.'
quests.exampleSentence: The CEO decided to spell SPELL OUT exactly which targets needed to be hit by December, rather than leaving things vague.
quests.example: The CEO decided to spell SPELL OUT exactly which targets needed to be hit by December, rather than leaving things vague.
quests.particleInsight: The particle 'SPELL OUT' combines with the verb 'SPELL' to specialize or transform its action.
quests.literalVsFigurative: Figurative, as before — the phrase describes explaining something so explicitly that no ambiguity remains.
quests.nativeTip: This means stating something with total, explicit clarity, leaving nothing vague or open to interpretation.
quests.visualAnchor: 🗝️ SPELL + SPELL OUT ➔ SPELL SPELL OUT

quests.definition: 'Sign over (something)' means to formally transfer legal ownership, typically through a signed legal document, such as property passing to a family member.
quests.exampleSentence: He signed the house OVER to his daughter before he passed away.
quests.example: He signed the house OVER to his daughter before he passed away.
quests.particleInsight: The particle 'OVER' combines with the verb 'SIGN' to specialize or transform its action.
quests.literalVsFigurative: Literal in the sense that a real signature is genuinely required to complete the legal transfer.
quests.nativeTip: This means formally transferring legal ownership of something through a signed document.

quests.definition: 'Hand over (something)' means to transfer control or responsibility to someone else, more broadly than 'sign over,' which specifically implies a formal legal document.
quests.exampleSentence: The outgoing president handed OVER power to his successor in a peaceful ceremony.
quests.example: The outgoing president handed OVER power to his successor in a peaceful ceremony.
quests.particleInsight: The particle 'OVER' combines with the verb 'HAND' to specialize or transform its action.
quests.literalVsFigurative: Figurative: nothing is always physically passed by hand — the phrase describes transferring responsibility or authority to someone else.
quests.nativeTip: This means transferring control or responsibility to someone else, in a general sense.

quests.definition: 'Handed over' fits an informal transfer of responsibility, confirmed by 'without any legal paperwork.' 'Signed over' would specifically require a legal contract, which the sentence explicitly rules out.
quests.exampleSentence: Because there was no formal contract involved, the founder simply handed HANDED OVER day-to-day control to his business partner, without any legal paperwork.
quests.example: Because there was no formal contract involved, the founder simply handed HANDED OVER day-to-day control to his business partner, without any legal paperwork.
quests.particleInsight: The particle 'HANDED OVER' combines with the verb 'HAND' to specialize or transform its action.
quests.literalVsFigurative: Figurative, as before — the phrase describes an informal transfer of responsibility between two people.
quests.nativeTip: This means informally transferring day-to-day responsibility, without any legal contract involved.
quests.visualAnchor: 🗝️ HAND + HANDED OVER ➔ HAND HANDED OVER

quests.definition: 'Pass on (something)' means to casually decline an offer, often used in relaxed, everyday conversation rather than formal writing.
quests.exampleSentence: Thanks for the invite, but I think I'll pass ON the party this time.
quests.example: Thanks for the invite, but I think I'll pass ON the party this time.
quests.particleInsight: The particle 'ON' combines with the verb 'PASS' to specialize or transform its action.
quests.literalVsFigurative: Figurative: nothing is physically passed to anyone — the phrase describes declining an offer in a light, casual way.
quests.nativeTip: This means casually declining something offered to you, in a relaxed, informal tone.

quests.definition: 'Turn down' is the more standard, neutral choice for formal written communication, unlike 'pass on,' which feels noticeably more casual and spoken, less suited to an official email.
quests.exampleSentence: In her formal email declining the invitation, she wrote that she would have to TURN DOWN the generous offer due to a scheduling conflict.
quests.example: In her formal email declining the invitation, she wrote that she would have to TURN DOWN the generous offer due to a scheduling conflict.
quests.particleInsight: The particle 'TURN DOWN' combines with the verb 'TURN' to specialize or transform its action.
quests.literalVsFigurative: Figurative, as before — the phrase describes declining an offer, expressed here in more formal, professional language.
quests.nativeTip: This means declining an offer, in language appropriate for formal written communication.
quests.visualAnchor: 🗝️ TURN + TURN DOWN ➔ TURN TURN DOWN

quests.definition: This reinforces 'pass on' in the same casual, spoken register as earlier in this level, here declining an evening plan due to tiredness.
quests.exampleSentence: I'm exhausted, so I think I'll pass ON drinks tonight.
quests.example: I'm exhausted, so I think I'll pass ON drinks tonight.
quests.particleInsight: The particle 'ON' combines with the verb 'PASS' to specialize or transform its action.
quests.literalVsFigurative: Figurative, as before — the phrase describes a light, casual decision to decline something.
quests.nativeTip: This means casually declining something because you're too tired, in a relaxed, spoken tone.

quests.definition: This revisits the LET family from earlier in this file. 'Let off' fits excusing someone from a deserved punishment, distinct from 'let down' (disappoint) and 'let go' (dismiss from a job).
quests.exampleSentence: Even though company policy would have justified serious punishment, the manager decided to let the intern OFF with just a verbal warning.
quests.example: Even though company policy would have justified serious punishment, the manager decided to let the intern OFF with just a verbal warning.
quests.particleInsight: The particle 'OFF' combines with the verb 'LET' to specialize or transform its action.
quests.literalVsFigurative: Figurative, as before — the phrase describes a punishment being reduced or waived rather than fully enforced.
quests.nativeTip: This means excusing someone from a deserved punishment with a lighter consequence instead.

quests.definition: This revisits SIGN OVER vs HAND OVER from earlier in this file. The casual, informal nature of the exchange — 'without any written agreement' — clearly points to 'handed over' rather than the legally formal 'signed over.'
quests.exampleSentence: Since it was just a friendly favor between neighbors rather than a real business transaction, she simply handed HANDED OVER the extra key without any written agreement.
quests.example: Since it was just a friendly favor between neighbors rather than a real business transaction, she simply handed HANDED OVER the extra key without any written agreement.
quests.particleInsight: The particle 'HANDED OVER' combines with the verb 'HAND' to specialize or transform its action.
quests.literalVsFigurative: Figurative, as before — the phrase describes an informal transfer of an object between two people who trust each other.
quests.nativeTip: This means an informal transfer between neighbors, without any legal document involved.
quests.visualAnchor: 🗝️ HAND + HANDED OVER ➔ HAND HANDED OVER

quests.conceptTitle: Phrasal Anatomy: CALL A SPADE A SPADE
quests.definition: 'Call a spade a spade' means to speak plainly and directly about something, without euphemism or avoidance. It's a fitting idiom to close this file, which has explored so many shades of formal, informal, casual, and direct language.
quests.exampleSentence: Rather than dancing around the issue with polite language, the new director prefers to call A SPADE A SPADE and address problems head-on.
quests.example: Rather than dancing around the issue with polite language, the new director prefers to call A SPADE A SPADE and address problems head-on.
quests.particleInsight: The particle 'A SPADE A SPADE' combines with the verb 'CALL' to specialize or transform its action.
quests.literalVsFigurative: Fully figurative: no actual spades are involved — the phrase compares calling something by its honest, plain name to naming a simple tool exactly what it is.
quests.nativeTip: This means speaking plainly and directly about something, without softening it with polite or vague language.
quests.visualAnchor: 🗝️ CALL + A SPADE A SPADE ➔ CALL A SPADE A SPADE
